title: Eventual periodicity of linear generalized Stone–Wales paths in affine fullerene families with convex lattice-face decompositions: paper and verification packet
description:
Paper (v6.3) and verification packet (lines 1.10.0). For fullerene families built from a fixed number of convex lattice faces with affine coordinates, existence of a literal linear generalized Stone–Wales path is eventually periodic along every integer affine ray (Theorem 1a, Corollary 1b). A formal version of Theorem 1a is proved in Lean 4 (standard axioms only, checked with Comparator); a prose lemma in the paper connects the paper's geometric hypotheses to it. For Graver's families K3 and C1 the ray results and their closed classifications are Lean-proved with no prose step; for O2 the ray result and the absence of paths for t, d ≥ 2 are Lean-proved with no prose step, for D14 the ray result is Lean-proved with no prose step, and for E10 the ray result (including r = 1, through the formal Theorem 1a) and the closed classification for r ≥ 2 are Lean-proved with no prose step. For D12 the closed classification and the ray result are Lean-proved with no prose step; two earlier, separately developed prose/computer-assisted proofs of the classification are kept as additional evidence. No human peer review; novelty is not settled.

The research was carried out with AI systems (OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code); the author directed the work and is responsible for it.
